fields.statement: At fdbebe1e I built rhiza with go build into a scratch dir and ran it by hand in a scratch git repo, with RHIZA_* and REX_* unset and a fake rex that logs its calls (no agent ever answers). rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual --once printed 'Started a run of <cs>' and exited. ps showed the driver 'rhiza run start --foreground <cs> --permission-mode manual' with PPID 1 in its own session. rex.log had only 'session ls' and the builder's own window new, no window new for the driver. The log was .git/rhiza/logs/<run>.log (no start-N file left) and held the child's 'step build/build: entered' line, and run ls --json showed the run running and live after the daemon exited. Under a long-lived rhiza daemon I killed a driver it had started: the pid was gone at once (reaped, no zombie), the run turned interrupted, and the daemon resumed it once as a detached 'rhiza run resume --foreground <run>' child of its own. After a second kill it was reaped too and the inbox listed the run as gave-up, with one daemon-resumed entry. rhiza request 'Add a widget' made the daemon start 'rhiza run start --foreground --workflow plan --new Add a widget --request <request>' detached, logging to <plan run>.log.

At fdbebe1e I built rhiza with go build into a scratch dir and ran it by hand in a scratch git repo, with RHIZA_* and REX_* unset and a fake rex that logs its calls (no agent ever answers). After the first run of the change set was abandoned, rhiza run start <cs> --permission-mode manual printed 'Queued a ship-change run of <cs> for the daemon: no daemon runs, so it waits for one (rhiza daemon)' and wrote starts.json. A long-lived rhiza daemon then started it headless as a detached 'rhiza run start --foreground <cs>' child, drained the queue (starts: null) and opened no Rex tab for the driver.

At fdbebe1e I built rhiza with go build into a scratch dir and ran it by hand in a scratch git repo, with RHIZA_* and REX_* unset and a fake rex that logs its calls (no agent ever answers). On a run the daemon had given up on (interrupted again after its one resume), rhiza run resume <run> with a live daemon printed 'Queued the continuation of run <run> for the daemon: daemon rhiza:<pid> continues it headless'. The daemon then ran a detached 'rhiza run resume --foreground <run>' child in its own session, with no rex window new for it. run ls showed the run running, and its log gained another 'continuing visit 1' line.

At fdbebe1e I built rhiza with go build into a scratch dir and ran it by hand in a scratch git repo, with RHIZA_* and REX_* unset and a fake rex that logs its calls (no agent ever answers). Two daemon starts of the same change set (the first abandoned, the second queued) logged to <run1>.log and <run2>.log. rhiza run log <run1> --all showed only builder session 475ed046 and <run2> only 50641ced, so neither log showed the other's lines (this was the cycle-1 finding). A daemon resume and a queued continuation appended to <run2>.log. A request's plan run logged to <plan run>.log, and rhiza run log <plan run> --all printed its 'step interview: entered' lines. With the log file moved away, rhiza run log <run> said it has no log and exited 2.

At fdbebe1e I built rhiza with go build into a scratch dir and ran it by hand in a scratch git repo, with RHIZA_* and REX_* unset and a fake rex that logs its calls (no agent ever answers). Every rex window new in rex.log came from an agent session: 'window new -s rhiza-qa qa: Built · run <run> · build/build · builder built-leaf #1' for each ship run, and 'window new -s rhiza-qa qa: Add a widget · run <run> · interview' for the plan run. Each named the repo session, the run and the step, and rex.log had no split at all.
